title: Contract Pricing Agreement: Reviewed Escalation Decisions on Pending Price Claims
content:
# Pending price claims decided on a reviewed escalation — Contract Pricing Agreement

**The rule.** This policy decides a price claim still pending on a Contract Pricing Agreement for an item whose latest price line is an annual escalation, reviewing that escalation, and records on the decision the unit price the agreement sets for the claimed line as this policy reviews the escalation.

**Current basis.** For the claimed line of an escalation this policy reviews on a pending claim, and only for such a line, the price the agreement sets is the reviewed escalated price this policy works out; the price of every other billed line is still the price in effect on the line's ship date under the tier's price change effective basis, chosen in this order: first, the item's contract unit price from the latest contract item price line for that item effective on or before the ship date, unless that latest line is a removal; otherwise, on a cost-plus tier, Corbett's supplier cost on the ship date increased by the tier's cost-plus markup percent with at least the tier's minimum markup per unit; otherwise, for a non-stock special-order item, supplier cost increased by the tier's special-order markup percent; otherwise, list price less the item category's discount from the tier's category discount schedule, or less the tier's flat list discount when the category is not in the schedule.

For an escalation this policy reviews on a pending claim, and only for such an escalation, the price the agreement sets is the reviewed escalated price this policy works out; every other escalation still raises a contract unit price by the percentage increase in Corbett's supplier cost for that item since the item's previous price line, capped at the tier's annual escalation cap percent of the prior contract unit price, and each item is still escalated at most once in any 12 months; a supplier cost decrease still never lowers a fixed contract price.

**The decision.** The decision is referred to the Pricing Desk when the overbilling, which is the claimed quantity multiplied by the difference between the billed unit price and that unit price, exceeds the tier's desk authority, and denied when the billed unit price is at or below that unit price or the overbilling is below the tier's smallest claim amount. It records the claimed quantity, the billed unit price, that unit price and a claim amount of 0.00. A claim the desk could approve is decided under the agreement's contract price claim rules instead.

**What the recording does.** One decision line is recorded for the claim named on the agreement's price claim records, carrying the claim's invoice number and item number as filed, the quantity, the billed unit price, the unit price the agreement sets as decided, a credited amount of zero, the decision and the day it is recorded. No credit is issued by this recording. The customer sees the claim's status change from pending to the decision recorded.

## Invocation

An agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `decide_pending_price_claim_4f6327a3` and then calls it.

| Parameter | Meaning and format |
|---|---|
| `pricing_agreement_id` | Reference number of the customer's Contract Pricing Agreement, read from the pricing agreement lookup (id) |
| `claim_reference` | The price claim reference exactly as the agreement's price claim records show it on the pending filing, copied character for character |
| `outcome` | The decision recorded, exactly one of: `denied` (the billed unit price is at or below the unit price the agreement sets, or the overbilling is below the tier's smallest claim, so nothing is owed); `referred_to_pricing_desk` (the overbilling exceeds what the support desk may approve, so the claim goes to the Pricing Desk for review) |
| `quantity` | The quantity decided, in integer selling units |
| `billed_unit_price` | The unit price billed on the claimed invoice line, USD, 4 decimal places |
| `contract_unit_price` | The unit price the agreement sets for the claimed line as decided, USD, 4 decimal places, rounded half up |

## Return

On success: `status` ("decided" when the decision line was written), `price_claim_id` (reference number of the new decision line), `claim_reference` (the claim decided), `outcome` (the decision recorded), `contract_unit_price` (USD, 4 decimal places) and `claim_amount` (USD, 2 decimal places, always zero on these decisions).
